messages:
simon: RFC follow-up: we still need a clear boundary between observers and the arbiter for canary/A-B flips. Two options: observers keep transient 'can-promote' state and act, or arbiter is the single source of promotion truth. I'm worried about accidental double-promotes during partitions.

jen: +1 to minimizing authority on observers. My vote: arbiter holds the canonical promotion lease. Observers should stream telemetry and can request provisional moves, but only the arbiter can issue final routing changes. Observers should be able to show a provisional UI state but not alter global routing.

mike: I'm sympathetic but worried about latency and scale. If every observer consults arbiter synchronously our p99 for canary reaction increases. Can we allow observers to do a limited, reversible provisional divert while arbiter asynchronously validates?

sasha: That matches a 'soft-promote' pattern I've been sketching. Observer can request a provisional diversion token and apply to a tiny fraction (e.g., <=1%) for quick smoke tests. Token must be replay-safe and scoped to tenant+route. Arbiter then collects signals and either upgrades to final lease or revokes provisional. Observers revert automatically on revoke/expiry.

simon: Proposal sketch for timings and limits:
```
provisional_ttl = 15s           # local soft-divert window
final_lease_ttl = 30s           # canonical lease duration
max_provisional_fraction = 0.01 # fraction of tenant traffic for provisional
reconcile_window = 8s           # how long arbiter waits for telemetry
min_samples = 500               # require this many samples before finalizing
```

jen: Token design idea: HMAC-based promo_token = HMAC(secret_k, observer_id|route|nonce|expiry). Arbiter verifies HMAC and checks nonce/expiry. To prevent global nonce storage, use per-observer monotonic counters persisted occasionally; arbiter only needs last-seen-counter per-observer. That keeps storage tiny.

mike: Alternative: signed short-lived JWTs with jti and short expiry (few seconds). JTI collisions are unlikely; for strict replay protection we can keep a ringbuffer of recent jtis per shard. If customers need absolute non-replay, enable exact-ttl nonce store.

sasha: On metrics: we must be explicit about the decision surface. Example rule we discussed: error_rate < 0.4% AND p90_latency_delta <= +100ms AND samples >= min_samples. Use delta comparisons against baseline, not absolute p90 in some cases. Also require consistent signal across >= 3 observers for the same tenant to avoid single-node bias.

simon: Good call on multi-observer quorum. For reconcile we should do a quick aggregation: collect (count, errors, p90) from observers, compute weighted aggregate, then compare. If quorum not reached within reconcile_window, revoke provisional.

mike: Storage/perf notes: keeping per-observer last-counter and per-tenant provisional record in arbiter is lightweight. The heavy path is global sample aggregation — do streaming sketches (TDigest for percentiles, reservoir sampling for counts). That keeps memory bounded.

jen: Operator UX: add a protected endpoint to force-finalize a promotion (RBAC + explicit audit log). Also add a Console banner when any provisional promotions exist and a link to the reconcile trace.

sasha: Observers must include provenance fields with every metric: observer_id, route, provisional_token (if used), sample_window_start. Make telemetry idempotent-safe. Use event ids for traceability.

simon: Failover semantics: if arbiter becomes unreachable, observers must not auto-promote beyond provisional_ttl. They should expire tokens and revert. If the arbiter is partitioned but later reconciles, it can accept or reject based on collected telemetry and audit proofs. No backwards-in-time promotes.

deploy-bot: canary-controller v2.4 rolled to staging at 1767130010 :rocket:

jen: Next steps: I'll write an Appendix with token formats (HMAC example + JWT option), and the reconcile aggregation pseudo-code. Mike will prototype TDigest hook in the observer shim. Simon will draft the sequence diagram showing provisional->final flow and revocation. Sasha will add telemetry contract fields and sample-sourcing rules.

simon: OK I'll add this to the arch repo under "canary-orchestration/provisional-flow". If anyone objects to the per-observer monotonic counter approach speak up now. Otherwise we'll include both HMAC and JWT patterns as selectable implementations. :thumbsup:
